description: Plan v7 section 8.3 fixture family 'm3b-wildcard-preference'. Inputs only; the oracle emits expected.

cases.notes: DefaultStrings.matchFor:1845, TRUE arm, discriminated. '*-CH' structurally filters to [de-CH, fr-CH] -- two different primary languages -- so the leading-wildcard rule has a real choice. preferredLocaleForWildcard must be used: the fallback locale fr is not itself a candidate, so it consults the FALLBACK LANGUAGE's tiebreaker list ['fr-CH','fr'] and selects fr-CH. preferredLocaleForRange, the other arm, would derive no primary language from '*', find no tiebreaker list, find the fallback locale absent from the candidates, and return the first candidate de-CH. The two arms therefore name DIFFERENT catalogs for one input, which the existing '*-ch' row could not do because its candidate list had a single member.

The FALSE arm of the same line, discriminated. 'de-*' filters to [de-CH, de-DE]; preferredLocaleForRange consults the RANGE's primary language 'de' and its tiebreaker order ['de-DE','de-CH'], selecting de-DE, which is deliberately NOT the first candidate in supported-locale order. preferredLocaleForWildcard, the other arm, would look for the fallback language 'fr' among the candidates, find nothing, and return de-CH. Read with the row above, the pair pins WHICH preference function each wildcard shape uses rather than merely that a wildcard matches something.
